name: WebWalkerQA
description: A benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal. It evaluates the capacity of LLMs to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. The dataset contains 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world scenarios (conference, organization, education, and game domains) across over 1373 webpages. It includes both single-source and multi-source QA types to simulate different human web-navigation paradigms.

creator.name: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang

citeAs: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang. (2025). WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal. arXiv:2501.07572v3
rai:dataCollection: The collection pipeline involves: (1) Traversing official websites recursively, collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages; (2) Constructing queries based on the provided page information and specified role, such as focusing on the solo page or considering both pages simultaneously; (3) Verifying and filtering for legitimate queries that deviate from natural, human-like phrasing, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Root official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. The root page is initially identified through a Google search using keywords such as 'conference official website' or 'game official website', followed by manual filtering. For the education domain, official websites of various university computer science departments were chosen. The dataset systematically clicks and collects subpages accessible through sublinks on the root page.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Web pages are converted to Markdown-like format using Beautiful Soup. The web page's markdown content along with clickable HTML buttons (and corresponding URL) are extracted as observations for the current page.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o performs initial annotations to generate synthetic QA-pairs based on predefined rules. In the second stage, crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering to refine the final results. Human annotators can rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure the QA pairs are correct and consistent.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: After the synthetic queries are generated by LLM, human annotators verify and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure correctness and consistency. The annotation includes verification that queries require natural, human-like phrasing and that answers are short entities.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be available at HuggingFace Datasets. The paper mentions approximately 14k silver QA pairs that are not yet carefully human-verified but can serve as supplementary training data.
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size is limited to 680 high-quality QA pairs due to the complexity of queries in the web-agent domain. The dataset only utilizes HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons and does not incorporate visual modalities such as screenshots. The dataset is constrained to actions limited to 'click' to evaluate navigation and information-seeking capabilities. The dataset focuses on text-based reasoning abilities using a Question-Answer format.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to evaluate LLMs on their ability to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website. It can be used for: (1) Testing web traversal capabilities of LLMs; (2) Evaluating information-seeking abilities in web navigation tasks; (3) Training and fine-tuning web agents; (4) Integration with RAG systems to enhance information retrieval. The dataset evaluates both performance (question-answering accuracy) and efficiency (action count of successful executions).
